topic: Tell me about yourself, fresher version
hook: "Tell me about yourself" is not a biography question. Interview Sarthi drafts the four lines that work.

slides.title: "Tell me about yourself" is **not** a biography question.
slides.subtitle: Interview Sarthi drafts it from your resume in four lines.

slides.title: Four lines. That is all it needs.
points: Who you are now: degree, college, one line.
One project you are proud of, and what it did.
One skill you built on purpose, with proof.
Why this role, in one honest sentence.

slides.question: So, tell me about yourself.
slides.answer: I am a final-year CSE student from Pune. Last semester I built an **attendance app** for my department that 300 students used daily. That project taught me **Flutter and Firebase**, and it is where I learned to fix bugs from real user complaints. I am looking for a role where I can keep building products people actually use, which is why I applied here.

slides.myth: Start from school, mention every subject, end with hobbies.
slides.fact: Start from today. One project, one skill, one reason. Under 45 seconds. Let them ask the follow-up.

slides.title: Blank on this question in the real call? Interview Sarthi drafts it from **your** resume.
slides.caption: It hears the question and shows what to say, in English or Hinglish, about your real projects.

slides.title: 30 minutes free. No card.
slides.subtitle: Windows app. Then one-time passes in rupees. Nothing renews.

caption:
"Tell me about yourself" is not a biography question.

It is the interviewer asking: why should I keep listening?

Four lines are enough:
1. Who you are now, one line.
2. One project you are proud of.
3. One skill you built on purpose.
4. Why this role, honestly.

Under 45 seconds. Let them ask the follow-up.

Save this for your next HR round.
